claims.text: Machine-learning-guided optimization of sintering profiles and composition can reduce the required sintering temperature.
Machine-learning optimization can identify conditions that achieve full densification.
The identified lower-temperature conditions can avoid abnormal grain growth.
A data-driven model can optimize temperature profiles and dwell times using high-throughput experimental data.
A data-driven model can guide composition adjustments that facilitate lower-temperature sintering.
The proposed intervention produces a uniformly dense microstructure.
The proposed intervention minimizes unintended grain growth.
The machine-learning model can uncover complex correlations among composition, sintering conditions, and microstructural outcomes.
Optimizing the inferred correlations enables prediction of profiles that yield full densification at lower temperatures.
Lower-temperature ML-predicted profiles can preserve material integrity.
The proposed method maintains or improves density relative to traditional high-temperature sintering.
The proposed method maintains or improves microstructural properties relative to traditional high-temperature sintering.
Conventional sintering processes require higher temperatures.
Conventional high-temperature sintering often causes excessive grain growth.
Conventional high-temperature sintering has elevated energy consumption.
The method's effectiveness depends on the quality and range of the training dataset.
The method is likely to be most applicable to material systems similar to those represented in its training data.
